title: A project README that reads as an engineer, not a tutorial-follower
takeaway: Anyone can list a stack; the live link, the architecture decisions and what you learned are what a recruiter reads as proof of work.
sources: The mental model is simple: your portfolio is a proof-of-work system.
The architecture decisions section is what separates a junior portfolio from a mid-level one.
A project that cannot be seen running is not a portfolio, it is homework.

data.heading: README.md, condensed from the post's skeleton
lines: Splits shared holiday expenses in the fewest possible transfers.
Chose Postgres over MongoDB: a genuinely relational shape.
The naive settlement algorithm was unusably slow above nine people.

notes.note: What it does: one sentence, no jargon
If it is not live, it does not count
A trade-off you made, with the alternative named
One you got wrong signals intellectual honesty
